newsitem.title: USA: Northwest sees higher fuel, other costs.
newsitem.headline: Northwest sees higher fuel, other costs.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp said on Thursday that higher fuel costs, the federal ticket tax and a weakened Japanese yen hurt third quarter earnings, and it expects more of the same in the fourth quarter.
The airline reported third quarter profits of $253.9 million, up from $231.1 million in the year-ago quarter.
"Northwest's third quarter results were affected by the reimposition of the federal ticket tax, a sharp rise in the cost of fuel and a weakened yen," said Chief Executive John Dasburg.
"We expect to see the impact of these factors continue into the fourth quarter," he said.
Third-quarter revenues rose to $2.73 billion from $2.56 billion a year earlier, the airline said.

Third quarter passenger load factor rose to 76.8 percent from 76.7 percent a year ago. Northwest said. Revenue passenger miles were 19.31 billion, up 8.7 percent from 17.77 billion a year ago. Capacity grew 8.5 percent to 25.14 billion available seat miles from 23.17 billion. Cargo ton miles were up 2.9 percent to 581.8 million from 565.4 million.
Third-quarter system-wide passenger yield declined to $12.54 from $12.59 a year ago, Northwest said.
